advices.diagnosis: The OrderService class aggregates four distinct responsibilities (order lifecycle, pricing, audit, notification) resulting in a very high method count (NOM=26) and cyclomatic complexity (WMC=56). The method‑attribute graph is split into five disconnected components (LCOM4=5), indicating poor cohesion. While the class only uses four internal domain types (DCC=4), extracting the responsibilities will improve cohesion and reduce the god‑class smell, though it may slightly increase DCC as new service classes will also reference those domain types.

suggestions.title: Extract responsibility‑specific services

advices.risk_notes: Splitting the class introduces additional objects and may require updating all callers to use the new façade or to inject the specific services, which could break existing tests. The increase in DCC reflects the new service classes also depending on domain entities; if the project enforces a strict DCC limit, this trade‑off must be weighed. Careful integration testing is needed to ensure that stateful aspects (e.g., audit list, sent counter) remain consistent after delegation.
